source_text: Παντὶ δόγματι καὶ λόγῳ τῆς ἐν τοῖς οὖσιν ἀληθείας ἐχομένῳ παραφύεταί τι ψεῦδος· παραφύεται δὲ οὐκ ἐξ ὑποκειμένης τινὸς ἀρχῆς κατὰ φύσιν ὁρμώμενον ἢ τῆς κατ᾿ αὐτὸ ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἕκαστον αἰτίας, ἀλλ᾿ ὑπὸ τῶν τὴν ἔκθεσμον σπορὰν ἐπὶ διαφθορᾷ τῆς ἀληθείας τετιμηκότων σπουδαζόμενον. Τοῦτο δ᾿ ἔστιν εὑρεῖν πρῶτον μὲν ἐκ τῶν πάλαι ταῖς περὶ τούτων φροντίσιν ἐσχολακότων καὶ τῆς ἐκείνων πρός τε τοὺς ἑαυτῶν πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς ὁμοχρόνους γενομένης διαφορᾶς, οὐχ ἥκιστα δὲ ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς τῶν ἐν μέσῳ στρεφομένων ταραχῆς. Οὐδὲν γὰρ τῶν ἀληθῶν οἱ τοιοῦτοι κατέλιπον ἀσυκοφάντητον, οὐ τὴν οὐσίαν τοῦ θεοῦ, οὐ τὴν γνῶσιν, οὐ τὴν ἐνέργειαν, οὐ τὰ τούτοις ἐφεξῆς καθ᾿ εἱρμὸν ἑπόμενα καὶ τὸν τῆς εὐσεβείας ἡμῖν ὑπογράφοντα λόγον. Ἀλλ᾿ οἱ μὲν πάντη καὶ καθάπαξ ἀπογινώσκουσι τὴν περὶ τούτων ἀλήθειαν, οἱ δὲ πρὸς τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς διαστρέφουσιν, οἱ δὲ καὶ περὶ τῶν ἐμφανῶν ἀπορεῖν ἐπιτηδεύουσιν. Ὅθεν οἶμαι δεῖν τοῖς περὶ ταῦτα πονουμένοις λόγων διττῶν, τῶν μὲν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας, τῶν δὲ περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας· καὶ τῶν μὲν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας πρὸς τοὺς ἀπιστοῦντας ἢ τοὺς ἀμφιβάλλοντας, τῶν δὲ περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας πρὸς τοὺς εὐγνωμονοῦντας καὶ μετ᾿ εὐνοίας δεχομένους τὴν ἀλήθειαν. Ὧν ἕνεκεν χρὴ τοὺς περὶ τούτων ἐξετάζειν ἐθέλοντας τὴν ἑκάστοτε προκειμένην χρείαν σκοπεῖν καὶ ταύτῃ τοὺς λόγους μετρεῖν, τήν τε περὶ τούτων τάξιν μεθαρμόζειν πρὸς τὸ δέον, καὶ μὴ τῷ δοκεῖν τὴν αὐτὴν πάντοτε φυλάττειν ἀρχὴν ἀμελεῖν τοῦ προσήκοντος καὶ τῆς ἐπιβαλλούσης ἑκάστῳ χώρας. Ὡς μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ἀπόδειξιν καὶ τὴν φυσικὴν ἀκολουθίαν, πάντοτε πρωτοστατοῦσιν οἱ περὶ αὐτῆς λόγοι τῶν ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς, ὡς δὲ πρὸς τὸ χρειωδέστερον, ἀνεστραμμένως οἱ ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς τῶν περὶ αὐτῆς. Οὔτε γὰρ γεωργὸς δύναιτ᾿ ἂν προσηκόντως καταβάλλειν τῇ γῇ τὰ σπέρματα, μὴ προεξελὼν τὰ τῆς ἀγρίας ὕλης καὶ τοῖς καταβαλλομένοις ἡμέροις σπέρμασι λυμαινόμενα, οὔτε ἰατρὸς ἐνεῖναί τι τῶν ὑγιεινῶν φαρμάκων τῷ δεομένῳ θεραπείας σώματι, μὴ τὴν ἐνοῦσαν κακίαν προκαθήρας ἢ τὴν ἐπιῤῥέουσαν ἐπισχών· οὔτε μὴν ὁ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐθέλων διδάσκειν, περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας λέγων, πεῖσαι δύναιτ᾿ ἄν τινα ψευδοδοξίας τινὸς ὑποικουρούσης τῇ τῶν ἀκουόντων διανοίᾳ καὶ τοῖς λόγοις ἀντιστατούσης. Διὸ πρὸς τὸ χρειωδέστερον ἀφορῶντες καὶ ἡμεῖς προτάσσομεν ἔσθ᾿ ὅτε τοὺς ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας λόγους τῶν περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας· κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν δὲ τρόπον ποιῆσαι καὶ νῦν ἐπὶ τῶν τῆς ἀναστάσεως λόγων οὐκ ἀχρεῖον φαίνεται σκοποῦσι τὸ δέον. Καὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτοις εὑρίσκομεν τοὺς μὲν ἀπιστοῦντας πάντη, τινὰς δὲ ἀμφιβάλλοντας, καὶ τῶν γε τὰς πρώτας ὑποθέσεις δεξαμένων τινὰς ἐπ᾿ ἴσης τοῖς ἀμφιβάλλουσιν ἀποροῦντας· τὸ δὲ πάντων παραλογώτατον ὅτι ταῦτα πάσχουσιν, οὐδ᾿ ἡντιναοῦν ἔχοντες ἐκ τῶν πραγμάτων ἀπιστίας ἀφορμήν, οὐδ᾿ αἰτίαν εὑρίσκοντες εἰπεῖν εὔλογον, δι᾿ ἣν ἀπιστοῦσιν ἢ διαποροῦσιν.
orientation: Athenagoras opens his treatise by explaining why he will argue first for the truth of resurrection before explaining it, since false opinions must be cleared away before teaching can persuade.
pass_a_gloss: To every doctrine and argument that holds to the truth in the things that exist, some falsehood grows beside it; and it grows beside it not from some underlying principle, starting according to nature, or from the cause according to which each thing is what it is, but it is cultivated by those who have honored lawless sowing for the corruption of the truth. And this one can find first from those who long ago devoted themselves to concerns about these things and from the disagreement of those men with both their own elders and their contemporaries, and not least from the very disturbance of the things turned about in the middle. For such men left nothing of the true things uncalumniated, not the being of God, not the knowledge, not the activity, not the things following these in sequence and outlining for us the argument of piety. But some utterly and once for all despair of the truth about these things, and others distort it to what seems good to them, and others even make a practice of being at a loss about evident things. Wherefore I think that for those laboring over these things there is need of two kinds of arguments, some on behalf of the truth, and some about the truth; and the ones on behalf of the truth are for those who disbelieve or those who doubt, and the ones about the truth are for those who are well-disposed and receive the truth with goodwill. For the sake of these things, those who wish to examine these matters must look at the need set before them at each time and measure the arguments by this, and rearrange the order concerning these things toward what is fitting, and not, by seeming always to keep the same starting point, neglect what is proper and the place that falls to each. For as regards demonstration and natural sequence, the arguments about the truth always stand first before the ones on behalf of it, but as regards what is more useful, the ones on behalf of it come before the ones about it, in reverse. For neither could a farmer suitably cast the seeds into the earth without first removing the things of the wild wood that harm the cultivated seeds being cast in, nor could a physician put in any of the healthy drugs into the body needing treatment without first purging the evil present in it or checking the evil flowing in; nor indeed could the one wishing to teach the truth, speaking about the truth, persuade anyone while some false opinion lurks in the mind of the hearers and opposes the arguments. Therefore, looking toward what is more useful, we too sometimes put forward the arguments on behalf of the truth before the ones about the truth; and to do in the same way now in the case of the arguments about the resurrection does not appear useless to those considering what is fitting. For in these matters too we find some disbelieving utterly, and some doubting, and of those who have accepted the first assumptions, some are at a loss equally with those who doubt; and the most unreasonable thing of all is that they suffer these things having no starting point at all for disbelief from the facts, and finding no reasonable cause to say through which they disbelieve or are at a loss.

choices.why: The verb means to grow up alongside, capturing the parasitic image of falsehood attaching itself to truth.
Keeps the agricultural metaphor of sowing that runs through the passage, and 'lawless' renders the privative adjective literally.
The word means not falsely accused or slandered; the literal rendering preserves the legal metaphor of false accusation.
The preposition 'on behalf of' distinguishes defensive arguments for the truth from explanatory arguments about the truth, a distinction central to the passage.
The preposition 'about' marks explanatory or demonstrative arguments, as opposed to defensive ones, preserving the author's two-fold distinction.
The verb means to lie hidden in wait, conveying the covert presence of false opinion in the mind.

pass_b_english: Every doctrine and argument that holds to the truth about what exists has something false growing beside it. But this falsehood does not grow from some underlying principle that moves according to nature, or from the cause proper to each thing as it actually is. It is cultivated by people who honor lawless sowing for the corruption of the truth.

This can be seen first from those who long ago devoted themselves to thinking about these matters and from the disputes they had with their own predecessors and contemporaries, and not least from the very confusion of the arguments being tossed around in public. For such people have left nothing true uncalumniated: not the being of God, not His knowledge, not His activity, not the things that follow these in order and trace out for us the argument of piety.

Some despair of the truth about these matters entirely and once for all. Others twist it to suit their own opinions. Still others make a practice of raising difficulties even about things that are evident.

For this reason I think those who labor over these subjects need two kinds of arguments: some on behalf of the truth, and some about the truth. The arguments on behalf of the truth are for those who disbelieve or doubt. The arguments about the truth are for those who are well-disposed and receive the truth with goodwill.

Because of this, those who wish to examine these matters must look to the need at hand in each case and measure their arguments by it. They must also adjust the order of these arguments to what is fitting, and not, by seeming always to keep the same starting point, neglect what is appropriate and the place that belongs to each argument.

For when it comes to demonstration and natural sequence, the arguments about the truth always stand first, ahead of the arguments on behalf of it. But when it comes to what is more useful, the order is reversed: the arguments on behalf of the truth come before the arguments about it.

A farmer could not properly cast seed into the ground without first removing the wild growth that harms the cultivated seed being sown. A doctor could not put any healthy medicine into a body that needs treatment without first purging the evil already present or checking the evil flowing in. Nor could someone who wishes to teach the truth, when speaking about the truth, persuade anyone if some false opinion is lurking in the minds of the hearers and opposing the arguments.

So we too, looking to what is more useful, sometimes place the arguments on behalf of the truth before the arguments about the truth. And it seems not useless to do the same now in the case of the arguments about the resurrection, as we consider what is fitting.

For in these matters as well we find some who disbelieve entirely, some who doubt, and even among those who have accepted the first principles, some who are just as perplexed as those who doubt. And the most unreasonable thing of all is that they suffer this while having no basis at all from the facts for their disbelief, and while finding no reasonable cause they can state for why they disbelieve or are perplexed.

problems.why: Rare/archaic word; modern reader cannot place it. Likely means 'un-slandered' or 'un-misrepresented'.

fixed: The glossary problem about singular/plural alternation is a style preference, not a mistranslation; the English follows the source's alternation between singular and plural forms of λόγος, so no edit is needed.
The word 'uncalumniated' is indeed rare and archaic; the source ἀσυκοφάντητον means 'not falsely accused' or 'not slandered', so I replaced it with 'un-slandered'.

polish.changed: Clarified the two kinds of arguments by keeping the singular and plural forms consistent with the source, replaced the archaic 'uncalumniated' with 'un-slandered,' and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.
